text: Noticing a large mug of mead on the table, the newcomer drank from it so deeply and so often that Missus Fennel watched him with growing alarm. <break time="0.8s" /> When the guests asked about his trade, he answered with a mysterious smile that he was going to Casterbridge on business of a very special kind. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, instead of explaining, he began to sing a strange song whose verses were like riddles, telling of a trade that was the rarest one of all. <break time="0.8s" /> He sang that he tied his customers up and took them up on high, and then sent them away to a far country, all in a cheerful voice. <break time="0.8s" /> At first the guests could not guess the meaning, but slowly, one by one, they understood, and the room fell into a frightened silence. <break time="0.8s" /> The man in gray was the hangman, on his way to Casterbridge Jail, where a prisoner was to be executed the next morning for stealing a sheep. <break time="0.8s" /> Everyone had heard of the poor clockmaker, who had stolen the sheep in broad daylight because his wife and children were starving. <break time="0.8s" /> Strangely, the first stranger, still sitting by the fire, joined loudly in the chorus of the song, as if nothing in the world troubled him.
